english-literature.anth-open-advice.0004.all: Prayer Before Birth (MacNeice): unborn child's fearful prayers; imperatives, 'I am not yet born', litany of threats, mechanised/totalitarian world, ends with plea for life; irregular rhymed stanzas. Pair with e.g. Do not go gentle (Thomas) - defiant attitude to life vs fear; villanelle vs incantatory stanzas.

english-literature.anth-open-advice.0015.all: Half-caste (Agard): speaker protests at the term; phonetic dialect, mock-polite tone 'explain yuself', rhetorical questions, painting/music metaphors, no punctuation, irregular form. Compare e.g. Search For My Tongue or Do not go gentle for strongly held opinions, and passionate address.

english-literature.anth-open-death.0015.all: Do not go gentle (Thomas): son's grief at dying father; villanelle, refrains 'Do not go gentle', 'Rage, rage', four types of man; grief shown as anger. Compare with Remember (Rossetti) - sonnet, gentle acceptance of loss, 'Better by far you should forget and smile'.

english-literature.anth-open-death.0002.all: Remember (Rossetti): Petrarchan sonnet, dying speaker's address to beloved, imperatives, shift at volta from remembering to permitting forgetting; muted grief. Compare with Do not go gentle (rage) or Poem at Thirty-Nine (grief for father).

english-literature.anth-open-experience..all: Blessing (Dharker): water bursts from pipe in a drought; single intense moment; free verse, sensory imagery 'skin cracks like a pod', religious/'blessing' lexis, the 'roar' of silver; compare with e.g. Half-past Two or Hide and Seek for intense moment; structure of one long moment.

Half-past Two (Fanthorpe? actually U A Fanthorpe): adult retelling a child's detention; child's time-ignorance; 'Once upon a'; capitalised 'Schoolroom', 'Little Timetable'; free verse; childhood episode. Compare with War Photographer or Hide and Seek for retelling a dramatic event.
